title: TASC criterion catalogue
description: The criteria of the TASC specification as data: one entry per criterion id, each either in scope for the stated conformance level or excluded with a reason. Tools that audit, register, enforce or attest controls read this file instead of the specification's prose.

$schema.description: Location of this schema, for editors.

specification.description: Repository-relative path of the specification the catalogue describes.

specification_version.description: The specification version the entries were written against. It changes only by a deliberate edit, so a revised specification is noticed and the entries are re-read against the new text.

level.description: The conformance level whose scope `in_scope` records.

criteria.description: One entry per criterion id in the specification, in the specification's order.

criterion_id.description: The criterion's id exactly as the specification writes it, for example AC5.4 or SI2.

criterion_title.description: The criterion's title exactly as the specification writes it. Detail for readers who know the specification; never shown in place of the question.

in_scope_criterion.description: A criterion that states a requirement (MUST) applying at the catalogue's level.

question.description: The requirement as one question a non-technical operator can answer or understand. Plain language, no criterion id, no specification vocabulary, and written so that the answer yes means the requirement is met.

kind.description: How the requirement is shown to be met. gate: by a control that refuses work which breaks the rule. artifact: by a record, document or configuration that exists and has the required content. human-attested: by the statement of a named person, because no tool can read the answer.

minimum_rung.description: The weakest evidence the criterion accepts. exercised: the control has been seen to operate, for instance by refusing a change that deliberately breaks the rule. observed: the evidence was read directly from the repository or a connected system. asserted: a named person states it. A human-attested entry is always asserted, and no other kind is.

not_applicable_when.description: The verifiable fact about the system that makes the requirement not apply, in plain language. The single word never when no such fact can exist.

level_note.description: Optional. What the specification says about this criterion at other conformance levels, where that explains why the entry asks for what it does.

excluded_criterion.description: A criterion left out of the catalogue's level.

excluded_reason.description: Why the criterion is left out, specific to this criterion: for instance that the specification states it only as a recommendation, or which level it ties the requirement to.
